newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast prods up sharply with NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast prods up sharply with NYMEX.

text.p: Pipeline prices for U.S. West Coast products extended yesterday's rally Wednesday in line with sharply higher futures and local refinery problems, traders said.

The wholesale price for CARB regular unleaded gasoline rose $0.03 a gallon for the second straight day to trade at 68/69 cents gallon late today. Premium, or octane, gasoline stood $0.06 a gallon higher than regular grade.
The August gasoline contract that expires tomorrow surged 3.43 cents a gallon following key inventory reports which showed shrinking U.S. supply and higher demand.
A handful of refinery problems and rumors of shutdowns also forced buyers to raise their prices.
Traders said Chevron in Richmond, Calif., shut part of their gasoline-making unit, while units at Shell and Exxon were rumored to have more significant problems than first reported.
Other products rose two to three cents in line with CARB, traders said.
